taxonomyDefinition.definition: The AI-agent topic taxonomy defines the canonical coverage areas the newsletter tracks so editorial, discovery, and coverage-evaluation workflows can reason about whether an edition spans the major ways autonomous agents are built, operated, and verified.

coverageAreas.label: Agent Runtimes
coverageAreas.description: Frameworks, SDKs, control planes, and execution environments that provide the core runtime for autonomous agents.
signals: Agent SDK or framework launches.
Runtime APIs for long-running or resumable execution.
Control-plane capabilities for planning, state transitions, or worker coordination.

coverageAreas.label: Tool Use and Integrations
coverageAreas.description: Protocols, adapters, and practical integration patterns that let agents call external tools and systems safely and effectively.
signals: MCP servers, tool-calling APIs, or connector SDKs.
Browser, shell, database, or code-execution integrations.
Techniques for tool selection, tool grounding, or integration ergonomics.

coverageAreas.label: Planning and Reasoning
coverageAreas.description: Techniques and systems for decomposition, reflection, policy selection, and other runtime decision-making used by autonomous agents.
signals: Task decomposition or planner architectures.
Reflection, self-critique, or policy-improvement loops.
Decision policies that choose or revise the next step at runtime.

coverageAreas.label: Memory and Context
coverageAreas.description: Persistent memory, retrieval, and context-management systems that improve long-horizon execution and agent continuity.
signals: Retrieval or memory backends for agents.
State persistence, context windows, or episodic memory systems.
Knowledge refresh or grounding techniques that improve execution quality.

coverageAreas.label: Multi-Agent Coordination
coverageAreas.description: Delegation models, agent-to-agent protocols, and orchestration systems used when multiple autonomous workers collaborate.
signals: Supervisor-worker or planner-executor topologies.
Agent communication protocols or handoff standards.
Coordination runtimes for specialized worker agents.

coverageAreas.label: Evaluation and Observability
coverageAreas.description: Benchmarks, tracing, telemetry, and reliability tooling used to measure and debug autonomous agent behavior.
signals: Agent benchmarks, eval harnesses, or judge pipelines.
Tracing, monitoring, or replay tooling for agent runs.
Reliability metrics for tool use, task completion, or regression detection.

coverageAreas.label: Security and Governance
coverageAreas.description: Sandboxing, identity, permissions, policy controls, and hardening techniques that constrain or secure agent behavior.
signals: Sandboxing, capability scoping, or least-privilege controls.
Identity, authentication, policy, or approval systems for agents.
Mitigations for prompt injection, supply-chain, or tool-execution risk.

coverageAreas.label: Deployment and Adoption
coverageAreas.description: Operational reports, production guidance, incidents, and ecosystem state changes that show how autonomous agents behave in real deployments.
signals: Production incident reports, rollout learnings, or cost-performance tradeoffs.
Adoption trends such as star velocity, usage growth, or repeated operator endorsements.
Hosting, lifecycle, or platform changes that affect agent operations in production.

sourceCoverageMapping.rationale: X surfaces launches, integration tips, and ecosystem reaction quickly, so it is strongest for early release signals and fast-moving adoption narratives.
Repositories, releases, and code-level metadata are strongest for shippable runtime, integration, security, and observability capabilities.
arXiv is strongest for net-new techniques, benchmarks, and research-led changes to planning, memory, and multi-agent behavior.
Reddit is strongest for operator reports, integration friction, comparative discussion, and emerging adoption signals from practitioners.
Broader web discovery captures vendor docs, security advisories, launch posts, and operational guides that round out coverage outside the seed platforms.

changeTracking.updatePolicy: Any taxonomy-area or source-mapping change requires a version bump and a new changelog entry. Quarterly reviews that do not change taxonomy behavior only refresh reviewedAt and nextReviewAt for the current version.

versionChangeRules.major: Use a major version bump when the canonical area model changes in a way that would materially alter coverage accounting across most editions.
versionChangeRules.minor: Use a minor version bump when adding, removing, or materially remapping a specific coverage area or source-family association.
versionChangeRules.patch: Use a patch version bump for clarifications, examples, or rationale updates that do not change coverage evaluation behavior.

changelog.summary: Established the canonical AI-agent topic taxonomy and seeded source-to-topic coverage mappings.
changelog.rationale: Coverage checks need a stable, machine-readable taxonomy so the system can tell whether editions span the major capability areas autonomous agents depend on.
taxonomyChanges: Defined eight canonical coverage areas spanning runtimes, tool use, planning, memory, coordination, evaluation, security, and deployment.
Mapped the current source families and adapter ids to primary and secondary coverage areas for later coverage evaluation.
Adopted quarterly review and semver-based change tracking for taxonomy evolution.
